To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
abnormal phosphorylation of Serine 409/410 of TAR DNA-binding protein 43 is a hallmark of frontotemporal dementia with ubiquitin inclusions and amyotrophic lateralsclerosis.

a monoclonal antibody (mAb) against TDP-43 phosphorylated at Ser409 and 410 (pSer409/410) was developed and that the mAb pS409/S410 specifically stained TDP-3-positive inclusions in FTLD-U, FTLD-F, FTLD-TDP, FTLD-MND, FTLD-MBD, and ALS.

abnormal phosphorylation of TDP- 43 at Ser409/410, which occurs only in TDP-43 positive inclusions in the brain of patients with FTLD-U and/or ALS, is a novel diagnostic marker for FTLD-U and that the phosphorylated TDP-43 can be detected by mAb pS409-410.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the phosphorylation of Ser 409/410 of the TARDBP protein, which is a marker of FTLD-U and a potential biomarker for ALS.
a monoclonal antibody that can be used to detect abnormal TDP-43 phosphorylated at Ser409/410 in FTLD-U/ALS.
the development of an antibody that can be used for the specific identification of FTLD-U and FTLD-TDP, which are characterized by the accumulation of phosphorylated TDP-43.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TDP-43 phosphorylation is a pathological feature in FTLD-U/ALS, and that TDP-343 phosphorylation is an early event of TDP-343 pathology.
the mAb pS409/S410 is a highly specific antibody for TDP-43, and that the abnormal phosphorylation of TDP- 43 at Ser409/410 occurs in FTLD-U.
the abnormal phosphorylation of Ser 409/410 in TDP-43 occurs in FTLD-U, and is a key event for the formation of TDP- 43 positive inclusions in the disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
abnormal phosphorylation at Ser409/410 occurs during the process of pathological aggregation of TDP-42 in FTLD-U, ALS, and some other neurodegenerative diseases.
TDP-43 phosphorylated on Ser409/410 in FTLD-U or ALS is a pathological form of TDP- 43.
phosphorylation of TDP- 43 at Ser409/410 may be an important event in the formation of TDP-433-positive inclusions in FTLD-U.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phosphorylation of Ser 409/410 of the TDP-43 protein is a hallmark of FTLD-U and a marker of TDP-3.

TDP-43 pathology in FTLD-U is associated with a unique post-translational modification, phosphorylation at serines 409 and/or 410, that is not seen in normal cells and that may be a key step in the formation of inclusions.
